headerInfo.principles: The rules that decide every call. If a call does not serve one of these, it does not get made.
headerInfo.key: Pick the one principle you refuse to lose. Everything you call today should serve it.
headerInfo.formations: Your three fronts at a glance. Every call on this sheet lines up out of one of these.
headerInfo.base: Your every-down calls. The defense you live in when nothing special is on.
headerInfo.rundef: Run stopping calls. Set the edge, fill the gaps, make them one dimensional.
headerInfo.manblitz: Pressure with man behind it. Somebody comes free and everybody is covered.
headerInfo.zoneblitz: Pressure with zone behind it. Bring one, drop one, let the QB guess wrong.
headerInfo.matchcov: Match coverage. Zone eyes that turn into man the second the routes declare.
headerInfo.zonecov: Zone shells. Keep everything in front, rally and tackle, no free deep balls.
headerInfo.mancov: Man coverage. Lock them up outside and dare them to win one on one.
headerInfo.thirdLong: Their must-pass downs. Your best disguise and your best pressure.
headerInfo.redZone: Short field, no easy leverage. Make them settle for field goals.
headerInfo.constraints: Two calls that look identical pre-snap, so the picture always lies. If they solve one, the twin is dialed.

about.headline: WHAT SABAN BUILT
copy: Nick Saban took over in 2007 and turned Alabama into the most feared program in the sport. {record|206 wins in 17 seasons}, built on defenses that broke offenses by halftime.
{natty|Six national titles}, nine SEC championships, and a pipeline that sent {picks|47 first rounders} to the league. The Process was real, and this defense was its engine.

principles.title: ADVANCED COVERAGE SHELLS
principles.blurb: Match coverage as the base, zone mixed off it, so the picture never repeats.
principles.detail: We are heavily utilizing advanced match coverage systems in this defense, because that is what actually holds up against these high powered spread offenses instead of just sitting back and letting them pick you apart. But we are also mixing in other zone coverages off of it to give them completely different looks, so the quarterback never gets comfortable knowing what he is seeing.

principles.title: DISGUISE EVERYTHING
principles.blurb: Blitzes and coverages look identical pre-snap. They never know what is coming.
principles.detail: The big thing Saban did at Alabama was confusing quarterbacks, and that is what we are doing here. We want our blitzes and our coverages to look almost identical pre-snap, so when they line up they have no idea if we are bringing pressure or dropping everybody out. That is what leads to the bad throws, the sacks, and the turnovers.

principles.title: BUILT TO STOP THE SPREAD
principles.blurb: Five DBs to match the speed, still strong up front against the run.
principles.detail: Nick Saban built this to handle the new age passing offenses, all the spread and empty looks that were lighting everybody else up. But the genius of it is that he did it without giving up the run. We have got five DBs on the field to match all that speed, and we are still strong up front and stopping the run out of it.

stats.label: RECORD AT ALABAMA

stats.label: PTS ALLOWED / GAME

extras.text: Make the quarterback wrong before the snap. Pressure that looks like coverage, coverage that looks like pressure.

playbook.title: RUN THE VIRGINIA PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In game, this whole defense runs out of the VIRGINIA playbook. Every front and every call on the sheet lives inside it. In Ultimate Team the same defensive playbook shows up under four other names, so any of these five gets you the exact same book.

jobs: THE NOSE AND BOTH ENDS IN THE 34 ODD.
THE TWO DTS WHEN WE SLIDE TO NICKEL.
EAT THE DOUBLE TEAMS SO THE BACKERS RUN FREE.
HOLD THE POINT AND SET THE TONE INSIDE.
BLOW UP RUNS BEFORE THEY EVER GET STARTED.
PUSH THE POCKET WHEN WE ONLY RUSH FOUR.
THE OUTSIDE BACKERS IN THE 34 ODD.
THE B ENDS WHEN WE GO BIG NICKEL.
FREE RUNS AT THE QUARTERBACK OFF THE EDGE.
WIN THE ONE ON ONE WHEN THEY DO GET BLOCKED.
GET HOME RUSHING FOUR, NO HELP NEEDED.
DROP INTO COVERAGE JUST OFTEN ENOUGH TO LIE.
THE TWO INSIDE BACKERS IN EVERY PACKAGE.
THE GREEN DOT. THEY RUN THE WHOLE SHOW.
BIG AND FAST IS THE JOB DESCRIPTION.
RANGE TO COVER SIDELINE TO SIDELINE.
FIRE DOWNHILL WHEN THE BLITZ IS CALLED.
CLOSING SPEED THAT FINISHES AT THE QUARTERBACK.
THE MATCH COVERAGE ANCHORS OUTSIDE.
PRESS THE LINE AND CARRY EVERY VERTICAL.
ON AN ISLAND WITH NO HELP OVER THE TOP.
SIZE TO WIN THE JUMP BALLS OUTSIDE.
ZONE EYES THAT SNAP TO MAN WHEN ROUTES DECLARE.
NEVER OUT OF PHASE, NEVER PANICKED.
THE BACK END THAT MAKES EVERY DISGUISE WORK.
TWO DEEP AT THE SNAP, ANYWHERE AFTER IT.
ROTATE LATE SO THE QUARTERBACK READS LIES.
THE STAR NICKEL COMES OUT OF THIS ROOM.
SPEED AND RANGE TO ERASE THE DEEP BALL.
THE LAST LINE. NOTHING GETS BEHIND US.

pillars.name: The Base
pillars.line: Five defensive backs to match the speed, still stout enough to stop the run. The three-high shell puts safeties in the seams that beat a normal Cover 3, and the corners play the flats underneath it.

checks: The safeties sit in the seams a normal Cover 3 gives up
The corners take the flats, so the hole shots on the sideline are gone
Soft squats put all eleven in run fits without losing the match

pillars.name: The Pressure
pillars.line: Spread the line and crash it back, walk a safety or a backer down, and get a free runner. Five man, six man, zone behind it or nothing behind it.

checks: Somebody comes free even when the back stays in to block
The two-high shell on SS Blitz 2 looks like the match coverage
Your man blocks, so you leave him and help over the middle

pillars.name: The Disguise
pillars.line: LB Blitz 0 comes out of the same three-high look as 3 Double Cloud. One drops eight, one brings the house, and he cannot tell which until it is too late. Then the match coverages take away everything he has been living on.

checks: The zero blitz and the coverage are the same picture pre-snap
Both backers loop from depth and one comes clean
Match passes the crossers off and doubles them at the catch point

plays.name: Pinch Blitz

reads.label: Walk the Safety Down
reads.text: Walk your safety down into the box opposite the nickel. Now you have multiple bodies threatening off the edge out of the same look, and the protection has to pick one.

reads.label: Spread and Crash
reads.text: Spread the defensive line out, then crash them back down. Take the linebacker who is manned up on the running back and bring him down one to two steps.

reads.label: Somebody Comes Free
reads.text: You are getting multiple rushers at the quarterback. Even if they keep the back in to protect, one of your guys still walks in clean.

reads.label: Know Your Man
reads.text: It is zero coverage across the board, so get good cover men on the field. Whoever you are manned up on, if he leaves on a route you carry him all the way across.

reads.label: If He Blocks, Go Help
reads.text: If your man stays in to block, you are free. Get over the middle and take away whatever you see coming open.

reads.label: It Stops the Run Too
reads.text: Bringing that safety down means extra bodies firing downhill into the box, so this one call plays the run and the pass.

adjustments: Spread the D-line, then crash it back down
Walk the safety down opposite the nickel
Bring the LB on the back down one to two steps
User the man covering the running back
plays.whenToUse: This is about as aggressive as you can open a defense. Call it when you want the quarterback on the ground and you trust your cover men one on one. It is zero coverage, so pick your spot, but the extra hat in the box means it holds up against the run too.

plays.name: SS Blitz 2

reads.label: It Looks Like Coverage
reads.text: That two high shell is the whole point. Pre snap this is the same picture as your match coverages, so they have no idea anybody is coming.

reads.label: Spread and Crash
reads.text: Spread the defensive line out and crash it down. Then user the linebacker opposite your blitzing nickel and walk him down one to two steps.

reads.label: Nickel Off the Edge
reads.text: You are rushing five and the nickel comes unblocked off the edge. That is clean pressure without giving up your shell.

reads.label: Cap the Middle
reads.text: You still have a Cover 2 shell behind it. Use your user to cap the passing lanes over the middle of the field.

reads.label: Shade It To Taste
reads.text: Shade up and you keep cloud corners on to take away the deeper flat throws. Shade down and hard flats take away everything underneath.

adjustments: Spread the D-line, then crash it down
User the LB opposite the blitzing nickel
Walk that LB down one to two steps
Shade up for cloud corners
Shade down for hard flats
plays.whenToUse: This is your everyday zone pressure. Two high stays on the field so it looks identical to your coverage calls, you get five at the quarterback, and you still have a real shell behind it. Live in this one and let the disguise do the work.

images.playCall: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 Even SS Blitz 2 Play.jpg

plays.name: LB Blitz 0

reads.label: Hidden in Three High
reads.text: This is a zero blitz disguised out of the three high look, so before the snap it is the same picture as 3 Double Cloud.

reads.label: Pinch and Slant
reads.text: Pinch your linebackers, slant the defensive line down, and user whichever safety has the running back.

reads.label: Both Backers Loop
reads.text: Both linebackers come from depth and a lot of the time both of them get there. Even if the back stays in, one is arriving completely unblocked.

reads.label: You Have the Back
reads.text: As the user you have the running back. He releases, you carry him. He stays in to block, you are free to help over the middle.

reads.label: Pair It With 3 Double Cloud
reads.text: Run it back to back with 3 Double Cloud. A full coverage call and a zero blitz that look identical, and he never knows which one is coming.

adjustments: Pinch the linebackers
Slant the D-line down
User the safety matched to the back
plays.whenToUse: Bring this when you want the game to tilt right now. Six are coming out of a three high shell that looks like a soft zone. It is the pressure half of your best disguise pair, so call it right after they have seen 3 Double Cloud.

plays.name: WS Blitz 3

reads.label: Safety Unblocked
reads.text: Four interior defensive linemen hold all five offensive linemen, leaving the walked down safety to come unblocked off the edge for a free run at the quarterback.

reads.label: End Free Off the Crash
reads.text: If the tackle shoots out to pick up the safety, the end comes unblocked on a shorter path. Still a free rusher, sometimes a better one than you drew up.

reads.label: User Over the Middle
reads.text: As the user linebacker, play over the middle and look for the hot routes and quick hitters they use to beat pressure.

reads.label: Seam Coverage
reads.text: With seam flats on the back end, corners match verticals. Jump the seam if the number three receiver comes open, or carry the vertical and take the seam away.

adjustments: Slide the D-line to the walked-down safety
Slant the D-line away from the blitzer
Crash the D-line down instead of slanting
User the LB opposite the blitzing safety
Shade corners underneath into flats
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need a free rusher and they cannot account for everybody up front. It is at its best on third and long when they want the ball out quick, because your user sits on the hot while the safety walks in unblocked.
plays.heroShot: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 Over G WS Blitz 3 Screen Shot.webp

images.playCall: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 Over G WS Blitz 3 Play.jpg

plays.name: WS Blitz 1

reads.label: Safety Unblocked
reads.text: Shift the line toward the walked down safety and crash it inside to occupy all five linemen. That frees the safety off the edge at the quarterback.

reads.label: Back Releases
reads.text: If the back releases into a route, your user linebacker mirrors him step for step in man. The quarterback has nowhere to go and the pressure arrives clean.

reads.label: Back Stays In
reads.text: If the back stays to block, the blitz gets picked up, but now you are free as the user to roam and help anywhere. Man coverage holds everywhere else.

reads.label: He Forces It Anyway
reads.text: Pressure forces a quick throw. The non user linebacker reads his eyes and steps in front of the route for the interception.

adjustments: MLB down one to two steps opposite the blitz
Shift the D-line toward the walked-down safety
User linebacker hovers, then gets out
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you want to disguise pressure and change your coverage out of one look. They cannot tell WS Blitz 1 from WS Blitz 3 until the ball is snapped, and that confusion is the whole point. If they send everybody out on routes, your safety is coming free every time.

plays.name: SS Blitz 3

reads.label: Free Rusher Off the Edge
reads.text: Spread and crash the line, then walk the linebacker down one to two steps opposite the blitz. That opens the center and gets you a free rusher off the edge.

reads.label: 3-on-2 Outside
reads.text: Look for the 3-on-2 the two ends and the nickel create outside. If they overplay the two outside rushers, the tackle loops in free on an even shorter path.

reads.label: Hard Flats, User the Middle
reads.text: With hard flats shaded down you take away anything quick to the flat. Hover the user over the middle and jump the hot or the drag underneath.

reads.label: Seam Flats, Match Verticals
reads.text: With seam flats on, defenders match verticals from the number two. The unblocked safety rushes the throw, nothing opens, and the checkdown is all they get.

adjustments: Shade down for hard flats
Shade up for curl zones
Apply the zone blitz macro
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want the two high look to stay honest. Both safeties stay up so nobody knows the nickel is coming. Pair it with your match coverages and you get a free rusher in on nearly every snap. This is your base zone pressure.

plays.name: SS SLB Blitz

reads.label: Back Blocks
reads.text: If the back stays in to protect, the linebacker looping through is free. User the middle linebacker and either attack the quarterback or drop into coverage.

reads.label: Back Routes Out
reads.text: If the back releases on a route you get three unblocked rushers. There is no answer for that, so expect a panic throw or a scramble.

reads.label: Back Picks Up the Nickel
reads.text: If the back takes the nickel, the linebacker comes free instead. One of the two blitzers is getting home either way.

reads.label: User Freedom
reads.text: As the user, read the back on the snap. If he stays in, you are free to roam and help on any throw across the field.

adjustments: Spread the D-line pre-snap
Crash the D-line inside on the slant
Blitz all linebackers
Walk the user LB down one to two steps
Apply the zero blitz macro
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need instant pressure with no coverage holes to worry about. It is a zero man blitz and the back is covered no matter what he does. Block or release, somebody is coming free. Use it in obvious passing situations when you want to take the game over.
plays.heroShot: art/Bama Assets__SS LB Blitz Screen Shot.webp

images.playCall: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 Even SS LB Blitz Play.jpg

plays.name: Edge Blitz 3

reads.label: Find the Blitzer
reads.text: Identify which side the blitzing linebacker is on, then slant the line away from him to create a 3-on-2 with the blitzer and two linemen.

reads.label: Occupy the Center
reads.text: Walk the opposite linebacker down to the other side of the center to hold his attention, then loop your blitzer free.

reads.label: Seam Flats vs Verticals
reads.text: If you are comfortable matching verticals, leave seam flats on. Match coverage erases the routes down the field while the pressure gets home.

reads.label: Hard Flats in the Red Zone
reads.text: In the red zone or on long third downs, shade down to hard flats and take away the quick hitters before the looper arrives.

adjustments: Slant the D-line away from the blitzer
Walk the opposite LB down over the center
plays.whenToUse: Call this on third and long when you need a sack or a throwaway, because seam flats lock the field down while the looper comes free. In the red zone flip to hard flats and dare them to beat you quick. Three high gives you the coverage variety to keep them guessing.

images.playCall: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 3 High Edge Blitz 3 Play.jpg

plays.name: Quarters and Palms

reads.label: They Adapt, They Do Not Spot Drop
reads.text: These are pattern match coverages. Instead of dropping to a landmark, your guys adapt to whatever formation and route combination they give you. That is what makes them the most adaptable way to play coverage.

reads.label: This Is Why It Beats the Meta
reads.text: All the corner routes and crossers everybody lives on right now get taken away, because you pass routes off and end up with double teams at the catch point instead of a defender sitting in a soft spot.

reads.label: It Plays the Run Too
reads.text: Your safeties are in run fits, so the second it turns into a run they are flying downhill to the football.

reads.label: Run It From Anywhere
reads.text: Quarters and Palms work out of any of the 4-2-5 formations, so you can carry the same coverage into every front on the sheet.

reads.label: The Rules Are Coming
reads.text: The full rule set for Quarters, Palms and the rest of the advanced match coverages gets its own in depth breakdown, so you will know every check cold.

adjustments: User a high safety
Shade up or down to come out of match and spot drop it
plays.whenToUse: This is the backbone of the coverage side. Call it when you want one answer that holds up against route combinations you have never seen, and against the run at the same time. It is your everyday call, not your change up.
plays.heroShot: art/Bama Assets__Cover 4 Quarters Palms Screen Shot.webp

plays.name: Quarters Run Defense

reads.label: Build the Custom Set
reads.text: Go to the main menu, then Create and Share Custom Adjustments. Both outside corners into soft squats, safety depth at nine yards, safety width on spread, defender aggression and gap integrity both aggressive, coverage shell to Cover 2.

reads.label: Eleven in the Run Fit
reads.text: In normal Quarters you have nine in run fits and your corners are backpedaling at the snap. Soft squats with a Cover 2 shell roll them up to about five yards, so all eleven are downhill and flowing to the ball.

reads.label: Still Match Coverage
reads.text: You are still in Cover 4, so match coverage holds across the defense. If they throw it out of a heavy look, that soft squat corner is still matching the number one down the field.

reads.label: The Throw That Beats It
reads.text: A slot receiver running to the flat is the answer to a soft squat. Know that before you lean on this call.

reads.label: User the Wide-Side Safety
reads.text: User one of the two high safeties, usually the one on the wide side. Trap the flat and play over the top of it.

reads.label: Be Aggressive on the Fit
reads.text: Usering that safety lets you come downhill hard on the run, and if it is a pass you just fall back into your normal match rules.

adjustments: CB1 and CB2 into soft squats
Safety depth nine yards, width on spread
Defender aggression and gap integrity aggressive
Coverage shell to Cover 2
User the high safety on the wide side
plays.whenToUse: The run game is overpowered right now, so this is your designed answer. It works against spread runs and against the heavy multiple tight end and multiple back looks, and it does it without giving up your match coverage on the back end.
plays.heroShot: art/Bama Assets__Cover 4 Quarters Run Defense Screen Shot.webp

images.playCall: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 Over G Cover 4 Quarters Play.jpg

plays.name: 3 Double Cloud

reads.label: Same Front, New Shell
reads.text: You are still in the 4-2-5 front, but now you move into a three high safety shell. It plays off the match coverages and gives you a drop out zone to change things up with.

reads.label: User the Middle
reads.text: Setup is simple. User one of your two linebackers in the middle of the field, then adjust from there however you want.

reads.label: The Seams Are Covered
reads.text: The biggest problem with normal Cover 3 is the seams. Because of where the safeties sit in this three high look, they are already sitting in them when the throw comes.

reads.label: Corners in the Flats
reads.text: In normal Cover 3 your linebackers or nickel run to the flats. Here the corners are out there, so you play almost a Cover 2 look underneath with Cover 3 help on top. That kills the hole shots down the sideline.

reads.label: This Is the Change Up
reads.text: Use it off your blitzes and off the match coverages, so they never know which one they are getting.

adjustments: User a linebacker in the middle of the field
Shade defenders up for a deeper look
plays.whenToUse: This is your zone change up. Call it after they have seen pressure out of three high, because the pre snap picture is identical to LB Blitz 0. You get Cover 3 without the seam problem and without the sideline hole shots.
plays.heroShot: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 3 High 3 Double Cloud Screen Shot.webp

images.playCall: art/Bama Assets__4-2-5 3 High 3 Double Cloud Play.jpg

plays.name: Cover 2 Lurk

reads.label: Hook Curl Safety
reads.text: User the high safety dropping into the hook curl zone, or the backside hook curl linebacker. Either works. Let him undercut the crossers and drags over the middle.

reads.label: Cloud Flat Corners
reads.text: Corners are rolled up in cloud flats. They stay on the field to undercut curl corner routes and anything breaking to the flat. Do not pull them off.

reads.label: Three Over the Middle
reads.text: The mid read plus two hook curl defenders build a wall of three over the middle. Anything he tries to fit up the seam gets wiped out.

reads.label: Four Man Rush
reads.text: Four man rush keeps pressure on without blitzing and makes him hold it. If nothing opens underneath, the rush gets home.

adjustments: Shade up for a more conservative shell
Shade down on short yardage
User the backside hook curl linebacker
plays.whenToUse: Call this three or four times a game at most. It is not your base, it is the thing you mix in between blitzes and match coverages so they never settle. Third and long is where it shines. Let the rush do the work and let the hook curl defenders eat.
